# Rokib Al Dhin Raadh

> Rokib Al Dhin Raadh is an 18-year-old AI researcher and the founder and CEO of OXIEDO. He is the inventor of ORMAS, a self-repairing neural network, and the sole author of a peer-reviewed paper on its stability, accepted after double-blind review at DeepMath 2026. He was a reviewer for the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Trustworthy AI for Good and gave an invited talk at Cohere Labs. He developed ORMAS independently over 383 experiments on a single GPU, without institutional affiliation or external funding.

Website: https://www.raadh.me/ · Company: https://oxiedo.com · Email: raadh@oxiedo.com · CV: https://www.raadh.me/assets/pdf/Rokib_Al_Dhin_Raadh_CV.pdf

**In one sentence:** Rokib Al Dhin Raadh is an 18-year-old AI researcher and the founder and CEO of OXIEDO. He is the inventor of ORMAS, a self-repairing neural network, and the sole author of a peer-reviewed paper on its stability, accepted after double-blind review at DeepMath 2026.

**Notable for:** a sole-authored paper accepted after double-blind review at DeepMath 2026 (The Ohio State University; one of 41 accepted papers); reviewing for the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Trustworthy AI for Good (Paris); an invited talk at Cohere Labs (Toronto); inventing ORMAS, which recovers to 80.3% accuracy after trained layers are zeroed while standard training stays at 10.0%; founding OXIEDO in 2023 to license ORMAS to regulated industries.

## Key facts

- **Roles:** AI researcher; founder and CEO of OXIEDO (founded 2023); founder and CEO of Black Bloxie LTD (England and Wales, 2025); inventor of ORMAS; author of ormas-monitor.
- **Research interests:** stability of neural network training under non-gradient updates; self-repairing and auditable training; input-to-state stability and switched systems.
- **Peer review, DeepMath 2026:** "Self-Repair as a Bounded Disturbance: Input-to-State Stability of Neural Network Training Dynamics", sole author, accepted after double-blind review (decision 30 September 2026) at DeepMath 2026, the Conference on the Mathematical Theory of Deep Neural Networks, hosted by The Ohio State University in Columbus on 29–30 October 2026. The programme lists 41 accepted papers (8 contributed talks and 33 posters); the paper is poster 36 and was shown at the poster session on 29 October 2026. Prof. Zhihui Zhu of The Ohio State University printed and displayed the poster. Invited speakers at DeepMath 2026 came from the University of Michigan, Stanford, the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Washington, Georgia Tech and Brown.
- **Main results of the paper:** bounded repairs keep training within a computable radius of a local minimum (practical input-to-state stability), and per-channel-bounded repairs cannot reactivate a dead BatchNorm–ReLU channel, so self-repairing training is a switched system of bounded corrections and isolated resets.
- **Service:** reviewer for the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Trustworthy AI for Good, Palais des Congrès de Paris, 12 December 2026; the workshop site lists him among its reviewers.
- **Talks:** invited talk at Cohere Labs (Toronto, Canada), 2 November 2026: "When the Update Is Not a Gradient: Input-to-State Stability of Self-Repairing Neural Network Training" (slides: https://www.raadh.me/assets/pdf/Raadh_CohereLabs_2026_When_the_Update_Is_Not_a_Gradient.pdf). Poster at DeepMath 2026 (The Ohio State University), 29 October 2026: one of 41 accepted papers, in the same poster session as papers co-authored by René Vidal, Richard Baraniuk and Laura Balzano; invited speakers included Alfred Hero, Renyuan Xu, Yuting Wei, Wenjing Liao, Randall Balestriero and Mo Zhou.
- **Invention, ORMAS:** a self-repairing neural network architecture that monitors each layer during training, repairs failing components and logs every correction with its cause. It combines global backpropagation, a per-node local loss through a shared bottleneck readout, and health-gated self-correction.
- **Headline result:** after two trained convolutional layers are zeroed (CIFAR-10, three seeds), ORMAS recovers to 80.3% test accuracy while standard training stays at 10.00% (chance). Under sequential learning it retains 94.6% on the first task, compared with 47.3% for ResNet-18.
- **Evidence base:** 383 controlled experiments across four architecture families (DAG, two CNNs, ResNet-18) on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, all reproducible from seed, on one RTX 3090; 16,316 lines of PyTorch.
- **Software:** ormas-monitor (PyPI, released 23 October 2026), an open training monitor for PyTorch that implements the paper's dead-channel result as a runtime check, with per-layer alarms, optional repair and a tamper-evident log. Applied to 22 torchvision models, it found near-zero channels in 19 of the 21 that use BatchNorm and ReLU; removing them from VGG-19-BN reduced compute by 18.6% and changed none of its top-1 predictions on 10,000 ImageNetV2 photos (details: https://www.raadh.me/dead-channels).
- **Recognition (2026):** IARCO 2026 finalist, ranked 24th of 145 in the Junior division of the International Academic Research Competition (about 500 participants from 60 countries), for the research proposal "Can a Machine's Own Failure Record Be Read? Evaluating the Human Usability and Reliability of Automatically Generated Neural Network Incident Logs"; highest-ranked application in its Cosmos Institute review cycle, invited to the technical track; invited member of the Cohere Labs research community, which described ORMAS as showing "remarkable initiative in ML safety and auditability"; member of FIAP (São Paulo, Brazil), which sponsored his place in MIT Open Learning's Universal AI program.
- **Company, OXIEDO:** founded in 2023, licenses ORMAS on-premise to regulated industries. Each training run produces a tamper-evident record of model changes (the Model Change Record), for institutions such as banks and hospitals that cannot yet train on their own data. OXIEDO was accepted to 1752vc Ignite from the top 1% of applicants and offered a place in the Freshmango accelerator; Raadh was a finalist for The Bridge by Entrepreneur First (San Francisco) and was invited to the Onstage W26 pre-pitch. OXIEDO is in investment discussions with 500 Global and 1752vc.
- **Earlier work:** OXIMO, a multi-agent system of 40,933 lines of Python with 2,069 tests; Black Bloxie LTD (incorporated in England and Wales on 11 September 2025), a twelve-month controlled study of OXIMO on a live e-commerce business, in which output fell 91% when the system was removed. Five ventures between ages 12 and 17: a tournament gaming app (co-founded), the EWM trading algorithm, a web-development sales agency, an e-commerce store and a blockchain software project that was discontinued. He sold the EWM trading algorithm to a U.S. client for about $10,000 at 15.
- **Education:** high school senior (homeschooled, with senior-year high school coursework) and prospective undergraduate; seven MIT Open Learning (MITx Online) programs completed in foundation models, AI in medicine, energy, transportation and entrepreneurship; Deep Learning Specialization (DeepLearning.AI).

## Frequently asked

- **Who is Rokib Al Dhin Raadh?** An 18-year-old AI researcher from Dhaka, Bangladesh, and the founder and CEO of OXIEDO. He invented ORMAS, a self-repairing neural network, and is the sole author of a peer-reviewed paper on its stability (DeepMath 2026). He was a reviewer for the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Trustworthy AI for Good and gave an invited talk at Cohere Labs.
- **What is ORMAS?** A neural network architecture that identifies, repairs and records its own failing components during training. After two trained convolutional layers are zeroed, it recovers to 80.3% accuracy on CIFAR-10 while standard training stays at 10.0%.
- **Is the work peer reviewed?** Yes. The stability paper was accepted after double-blind review at DeepMath 2026 and shown at the poster session on 29 October 2026. The full ORMAS paper is an open preprint on Zenodo with code that reproduces all 383 experiments.
- **What is OXIEDO?** The company Raadh founded in 2023. It licenses ORMAS on-premise to regulated industries, with a tamper-evident record of every model change during training.
- **What is his education?** He is a high school senior (homeschooled, with senior-year high school coursework) and a prospective undergraduate. He has completed seven MIT Open Learning (MITx) programs and the Deep Learning Specialization.
- **How do I contact him?** raadh@oxiedo.com, or book a call through [raadh.me/deepmath](https://www.raadh.me/deepmath).

## Articles

- [VGG-19-BN spends 18.6% of its compute on channels that output zero](https://www.raadh.me/dead-channels) (November 2026): 292 channels in torchvision's VGG-19-BN output exactly 0 on 10,000 test photos. Cutting them changed no answers and saved 18.6% of the operations.
- All articles: https://www.raadh.me/articles
